stories.title: Cisco patches new Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks
stories.summary: Cisco has patched another actively exploited zero-day flaw in its Secure Email Gateway (SEG) that lets remote unauthenticated attackers execute commands with root privileges.
stories.explanation: Cisco's email security product had a flaw that attackers could exploit without logging in to take full control of the system. This matters because email gateways protect organizations from malicious messages, so compromising one gives attackers a foothold to send phishing emails or access company data. Defenders must apply Cisco's patch immediately and monitor their email gateway logs for suspicious activity.

stories.title: Palo Alto Networks Patches PAN-OS Zero-Day Exploited for Remote Code Execution
stories.summary: The company says it’s aware of limited exploitation against customers’ firewalls, and it has made IoCs available.
stories.explanation: Palo Alto Networks released a fix for a serious flaw in PAN-OS (the operating system running their firewalls) that allows remote code execution—meaning attackers can run commands on the firewall without authentication. This is critical because firewalls are the main barrier between your network and the internet, so compromising one is like unlocking your front door. Defenders should apply the patch right away and check provided Indicators of Compromise (IoCs—technical fingerprints of attacks) to see if they were targeted.

stories.title: Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
stories.summary: Palo Alto Networks has released security updates for a high-severity PAN-OS RCE zero-day, tracked as CVE-2026-0322, that has been exploited in attacks targeting firewalls.
stories.explanation: A high-severity flaw (CVE-2026-0322) in Palo Alto's PAN-OS allows attackers to execute code remotely on firewalls, and it's already being actively exploited in real attacks. Firewalls are critical defensive tools, so this vulnerability puts organizations at immediate risk of network infiltration and data theft. Security teams must prioritize patching this flaw and reviewing firewall logs to detect any compromise attempts.

stories.title: CISA warns admins to immediately fix Ivanti flaw exploited as zero-day
stories.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) urged security teams to immediately patch an Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) flaw exploited in zero-day attacks since at least October 1st.
stories.explanation: CISA (the U.S. government's cybersecurity agency) issued an urgent alert about an Ivanti Connect Secure flaw that attackers have been exploiting since October without needing a patch. Ivanti appliances are remote access gateways, so this flaw could let attackers bypass authentication and access internal networks. Defenders should patch immediately, assume breach (meaning act as though attackers already got in), and review access logs from October onward.

stories.title: CISA Urges Immediate Ivanti Connect Secure Updates as Honeypots Log 105 Exploit Attempts
stories.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday urged organizations to take steps to immediately update their Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) appliances and deployments to the latest version following the disclosure of an actively exploited vulnerability. The security flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS score: 8.6), is a case of authentication bypass impacting ICS
stories.explanation: CISA warned organizations to urgently update Ivanti Connect Secure appliances after discovering an actively exploited vulnerability; honeypot systems (fake targets that log attacks) recorded over 100 exploit attempts. Ivanti products are often the first thing employees use to access company networks remotely, making this flaw a high-value target for attackers. Organizations must update to the latest version and investigate whether their systems were compromised before the patch was available.

stories.title: Palo Alto Networks Patches PAN-OS Authenticated RCE Flaw Amid Active Exploitation
stories.summary: Palo Alto Networks on Wednesday issued security updates for a high-severity flaw in PAN-OS software that has come under active exploitation. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0322 (CVSS score: 8.6), is a case of remote code execution in the management interface. stories.explanation: Palo Alto Networks patched a serious flaw (CVE-2026-0322, CVSS 8.6) in PAN-OS that allows authenticated users (or attackers with stolen credentials) to execute code on the firewall's management system. While this requires some level of access, it's being actively exploited and lets attackers gain full control of a critical security tool. Defenders should apply the patch immediately, reset firewall administrative credentials, and audit who has had access.

stories.title: Langflow's Critical Authenticated RCE Flaw Targeted in 1,423 Honeypot Exploit Attempts
stories.summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical security flaw in Langflow, according to an alert from Previdian. Langflow is an open-source platform that allows developers to build artificial intelligence (AI) applications and agentic workflows. stories.explanation: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in Langflow (an open-source AI platform by DataStax) to run unauthorized commands; honeypots detected over 1,400 exploit attempts in February 2025. Langflow is used by developers to build AI applications, so compromise could lead to malicious AI applications or data theft. Organizations using Langflow must patch immediately and review application logs for signs of unauthorized access.

stories.title: Hackers Backdoor Nextcloud Servers Through Critical Flaw in Collabora’s Built-in CODE App
stories.summary: Attackers exploited a flaw in an optional Nextcloud app, Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server, to plant web shells on Nextcloud servers. Three administrators reported the issue on GitHub, with the first logged attack on September 10. A web shell is a small file that executes any command an attacker sends via a web request, with the rights of the web server account. The flaw
stories.explanation: Attackers exploited a flaw in Collabora Online CODE (an optional app in Nextcloud) to install web shells (small malicious scripts) that give them ongoing access to Nextcloud servers. Nextcloud is a file-sharing platform, so compromising it gives attackers access to sensitive documents and the ability to backdoor the system for long-term persistence. Defenders should disable the Collabora Online app if not needed, patch if available, and scan for web shells using file integrity monitoring.

cves.name: ISC BIND Data Processing Errors Vulnerability
cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: CVE-2015-5477 is a data processing error vulnerability in ISC BIND (the software that translates domain names to IP addresses). Flaws in DNS software can allow attackers to disrupt internet connectivity or redirect traffic, affecting any organization relying on that DNS server. Defenders should update BIND to patched versions and implement DNS query filtering to limit potential impact.

cves.explanation: CVE-2015-3306 is an improper access control flaw in ProFTPD (file transfer software) that could allow attackers to access files they shouldn't have permission to view or modify. FTP servers often store sensitive files, so this flaw could lead to data theft or unauthorized modifications. Defenders should patch ProFTPD, restrict FTP access to necessary users only, and monitor file access logs.

cves.explanation: CVE-2016-3081 is a command injection flaw in Apache Struts (a framework developers use to build Java web applications) that lets attackers execute arbitrary commands on the web server. Any web application built with vulnerable Struts versions is at risk of complete compromise. Defenders must update Struts to patched versions in all applications, validate and sanitize user input, and monitor server logs for suspicious command execution.

cves.description: Authentication bypass by spoofing in ICS before version 25.1.3.0 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands. This does not impact ICS version 22.7R2.14 or prior.

cves.action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
cves.explanation: This Ivanti vulnerability (affecting versions after 22.7R2.14 but before 25.1.3.0) allows attackers to bypass authentication and run commands without logging in, exploiting a spoofing flaw (tricking the system into accepting false identity claims). Ivanti appliances control remote access to networks, so this flaw lets unauthenticated attackers gain entry to internal systems. Defenders must update to version 25.1.3.0 or later and verify that only legitimate users accessed the system before patching.

cves.description: Improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in Windows Shell allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

cves.explanation: CVE-2026-96951 is a command injection flaw in Windows Shell that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass security features and execute commands over the network. The Windows Shell is a core operating system component, so compromising it could give attackers broad control of Windows machines. Defenders should apply Microsoft security patches, implement network segmentation to limit Shell access, and use endpoint detection tools to catch malicious command execution.
